model.name: Model for renal canagliflozin, M5 and M7 excretion.

notes.body:
Model for renal canagliflozin, M5 and M7 excretion.
Canagliflozin is eliminated urine (33%, mainly O-glucuronide metabolites) [Deeks2017]
~33 % of the oral dose was excreted in urine (M5: 13.3 %, M7: 17.2 %, canagliflozin <1%) [Devineni2015h]
=> mainly renal excretion of M5 and M7, small excretion of can
The content of this model has been carefully created in a manual research effort.

body.p: Used for comparison with total radioactivity in urine.
Fasting plasma glucose (FPG). Model depends on the fasting plasma glucose:

ul.li: as a proxy of the daily glucose variation in the glucose excretion
to set the glucose dependent RTG values (i.e. T2DM have higher SGLT2 amounts, and consequently higher RTG values)

body.p: scaling factor for renal function. 1.0: normal renal function; <1.0: reduced renal function
Scaling factor to vary UGT1A9 activity in kidney. 1.0: normal activity; <1.0 decreased activity; >1.0 increased activity.
estimated EC50 value was 32 ng/mL (95% CI = 19–45 ng/mL). [Devineni2013]
Typical RTG value without SGLT2 inhibitors in healthy subjects.

pre.code: This corresponds to the SGLT2 concentrations.

body.p: Effect of the FPG on the change in RTG_base.
maximum inhibition of RTG via SGLT2

parameter.name: scaling factor CAN2M7 kidney vs liver

body.p: Scaling factor relative to liver UGT1A9 activity. 1.0 = equal to liver, < 1.0 = lower, > 1.0 = higher.
FPG dependent base RTG value. SGLT2 is induced in T2DM [Rahmoune2005]
ΔRTG, maximum reduction in RTG due to SGLT2 inhibition. Normally around 7 - 10 mM.

The renal threshold for glucose (RTG) is the plasma glucose concentration at which tubular reabsorption of glucose begins to saturate; glucose is excreted into the urine in direct proportion to the glucose concentration above this threshold. 12.3 - 12.7 mM RTG (placebo) [Devineni2012]
Urinary glucose excretion is calculated from cumulative amount of glucose in urine.
